name: How can I maximize every inch of my tiny home?

step.name: Step 1: Assess Your Belongings — Go through everything you own with a critical eye. What do you use daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly? What can you let go of? This step is crucial because efficient storage starts with less stuff. It helps you understand the volume and types of items you truly need to store.
step.text: Step 1: Assess Your Belongings — Go through everything you own with a critical eye. What do you use daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly? What can you let go of? This step is crucial because efficient storage starts with less stuff. It helps you understand the volume and types of items you truly need to store.

step.name: Step 2: Map Out Zones — Divide your tiny home into functional zones: sleeping, cooking, living, working, and bathing. Within each zone, identify where specific activities happen and what items are needed there. This clarity helps in designing integrated storage that serves a purpose. What it looks like done: a clear diagram of your home with designated areas for different life activities.

step.name: Step 3: Embrace Verticality — Look up! Walls are invaluable storage real estate. Think about floor-to-ceiling shelving, wall-mounted cabinets, and hanging solutions. This frees up precious floor space and keeps your living areas clear. What it looks like done: vertical storage solutions are sketched out for every wall, maximizing height.
step.text: Step 3: Embrace Verticality — Look up! Walls are invaluable storage real estate. Think about floor-to-ceiling shelving, wall-mounted cabinets, and hanging solutions. This frees up precious floor space and keeps your living areas clear. What it looks like done: vertical storage solutions are sketched out for every wall, maximizing height.

step.name: Step 4: Demand Dual Functionality — Every piece of furniture and every structural element should ideally serve more than one purpose. A bed with drawers, stairs with built-in cupboards, a dining table that folds away, or an ottoman that opens for storage are perfect examples. This helps your home adapt to various needs without adding bulk.

step.name: Step 5: Utilize Nooks and Crannies — Don't overlook awkward spaces. The area under eaves, behind doors, or in kickplates can all be transformed into clever, hidden storage. Custom solutions are key to making these often-wasted spaces productive. What it looks like done: every small, otherwise unused space has a custom storage solution designed for it.

step.name: Step 6: Plan for Access and Visibility — Think about how often you'll need specific items. Daily-use items should be easily accessible, while seasonal or less-frequent items can go into harder-to-reach spots. Good organization means you can find what you need without a major excavation. What it looks like done: all items have a logical, easily accessible home.
